solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: President with newspaper backing joining election candidates?

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the newspaper word is read from right to left

parts.note: a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
the field is the whole set of contestants in a race or election

explanation.surface: A presidential hopeful, propped up by a newspaper, joins the other candidates in an election.
explanation.walkthrough: James Garfield was the 20th US President. 'President' looks like it belongs to the election story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: James A. Garfield served briefly as American head of state in 1881 before being assassinated.

clue.text: Eat too much, so dreaming is awful

indicators.note: awful means terrible or badly done, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of both words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Fantasising about food so much that you overeat is a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To gormandise is to eat greedily and to excess, like a glutton.

clue.text: Managed to curtail row

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rank is a row, as in ranks of soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in cutting an argument short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it, so the past tense means managed.

clue.text: With devils around, death is threatening

indicators.note: something around another word wraps about it, so the devils enclose death

parts.note: imps are little devils
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: Surrounded by devils, death looms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends is about to happen, typically something bad, so it hangs threateningly over us.

clue.text: Sweet female who gets in the way

definitions.note: read as 'one who gets in the way'

parts.note: a lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A kind woman who is nonetheless always in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lollipop lady is a school crossing warden, named for her round stop sign on a pole, who steps into the road to halt traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossing patrol's job is literally to stand in the path of cars so children can cross.

clue.text: Mood of agent encountered on return

indicators.note: something on its return journey travels back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent for a firm
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone describes the mood of a secret agent they met on coming back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A temper is a state of mind, as in being in a good or bad temper, so it is a mood.

clue.text: Bigheadedness, energy and drive associated with male model standing up

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
go is drive or energy, as in full of go

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
to sit is to model, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: Vanity, energy and ambition go together in a male model striking a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the male model part is turned upside down; 'and' joins the first pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is excessive self-importance, which is what being bigheaded means.

clue.text: Meal unchanged? This is the wrapped meal you'll see

parts.note: surface reading: a meal left exactly as it is

parts.words: This is the wrapped meal you'll see
parts.note: setter's reading: look at the first two words and you see a midday meal tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A sandwich box brought from home, untouched and still in its wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'meaL UNCHanged' the word LUNCH is packed inside, so the clue shows a packed lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food prepared at home and wrapped up to be eaten at school or work.

clue.text: Bird to listen to — the last to fly up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, the final letter flying up moves it to the top, ahead of the others

parts.note: to hear is to listen

explanation.surface: Listen to a bird, the last of the flock taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhea cannot fly at all, which adds wit to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Gang with influence — one can provide an opening

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring
pull is influence, as in having pull with the boss; 'with' joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: A gang with clout can open doors for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'opening' sounds like an opportunity offered by powerful friends; it is the literal hole in a drinks can. 'One can' hides the pun: a can is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring pull is the tab on a drinks tin that you lift to open it.

clue.text: Disreputable yob, revolutionary for short time

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means a swap: the revolutionary goes in where the short time word was

parts.note: a lout is a yob, a rough uncouth young man
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A disreputable yob briefly turns revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the yob and replace its T, short for time, with the revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche describes someone of dubious morals or shady reputation, a synonym of disreputable.

clue.text: See a hesitant drunk get knocked out

definitions.note: causative: to make someone get knocked out

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of all three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Watch a hesitant drunk get knocked out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To anaesthetise someone is to render them unconscious with drugs, putting them out before surgery.

clue.text: India's sect, one involved in religious festival

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled or convoluted, so the letters get mixed up

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: An Indian sect and a member of it take part in a religious celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascensiontide is the Christian season marking Christ's ascent to heaven, forty days after Easter.

clue.text: Approach shortened for Scrooge — one makes concessions

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the approach word loses its last letter

parts.note: to come is to approach
pro means for, in favour of
Scrooge, from Dickens' A Christmas Carol, is the archetypal miser

explanation.surface: A shortened approach is used for Scrooge, who gives some ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who compromises gives up part of their demands to reach agreement, a person making concessions.

clue.text: Sweet talk perhaps to stop with emotions not head restricting chaps

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the chaps are enclosed
not head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: to end is to stop
the heart is the seat of emotions
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Perhaps sweet talk can halt emotions from running away with you.
explanation.walkthrough: The beheaded emotions word goes around the chaps, all after the stop.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is an affectionate word like 'darling', which is an example of sweet talk, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Casts off a feeling of melancholy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gets rid of, discards
second meaning: low spirits, as in being down in the...

explanation.surface: Someone sheds a mood of sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the idiom 'down in the dumps', meaning gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump is to discard, and the plural noun is an idiom for a depressed state of mind.

clue.text: What's gone wrong with lemon, bad fruit

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so the preceding word's letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: bad suggests spoiled or faulty, so the citrus word's letters are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what has happened to a lemon that has turned rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate shuffles: one word gone wrong, the other bad. The Ogen is a small melon variety bred in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ogen is a cantaloupe-type variety of the sweet fruit with green flesh.

clue.text: A very small volume of liquid running through highway?

definitions.text: A very small volume of liquid running through highway?

indicators.note: something running through a road passes inside it, so these letters sit within the highway word

parts.note: a street is a public road
taken as written
ml is a millilitre, a tiny measure of liquid

explanation.surface: A trickle of water flows along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: A plus the millilitre sits inside the road, and a tiny flow of water running across a road is exactly what is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamlet is a little brook, a small flow of running water.

clue.text: An eleven with no score — useless getting worried

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a cricket or football team is an eleven
no score is nil, shown as O; 'with' joins
u/s is short for unserviceable, meaning useless

explanation.surface: A sports team that has not scored and is playing badly starts to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a cricket or football side; U/S, unserviceable, is a military abbreviation for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious means uneasy or fretful, a straightforward synonym for worried.

clue.text: Not the brightest — studies English!

parts.note: a den is a private study room
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A jibe that someone who studies English is not very clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' reads as a verb but is a plural noun for rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means slow-witted or stupid, an informal match for not the brightest.

clue.text: Philosophy of the Parisian boxer, seldom lacking guts

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'; 'of' joins
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

indicators.note: with its guts gone a word keeps only its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A French boxer's philosophy, one that seldom lacks courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the Parisian' asks for French for 'of the', which is DU.
explanation.definitionFit: Dualism is a philosophical doctrine dividing reality into two principles, such as mind and matter.

clue.text: Botched expression that could bring poet harm?

definitions.text: Botched expression that could bring poet harm?

parts.note: surface reading: a garbled figure of speech that combines incompatible images
setter's reading: jumble the letters of a figure-of-speech word and you get 'poet harm'

explanation.surface: A clumsy phrase could do a poet's reputation damage.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: MIXED METAPHOR, read literally, says to mix the letters of METAPHOR, which gives POET HARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed metaphor is an ill-judged phrase combining incongruous images, a botched figure of speech.

clue.text: Stuff made from dairy product with no indicator of additives

indicators.note: with no means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: cream is a dairy product
food additives carry E numbers

explanation.surface: A product made from cream that is free of additives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Europe approved food additives carry codes like E621, so E signals an additive.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to stuff, pack something tightly full.

clue.text: Remain outside house as one who's faced the cameras again?

definitions.text: one who's faced the cameras again?
definitions.note: a cryptic stretch: the answer is an adjective/participle for what has been filmed again, not a person

indicators.note: one word standing outside another wraps around it

parts.note: to rest is to remain, stay put
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay outside the house as if they are a film star returning to the cameras.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reshot has been filmed a second time, so an actor in it has gone before the cameras again.

clue.text: Cut down on one entrance at back of university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone is told to use one entrance at the rear of a campus less often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At back of' puts the one and the entrance after the university.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to lessen or reduce something's severity, a synonym of cutting down on.

clue.text: Hail in road briefly

indicators.note: briefly means in short form, so the road word is abbreviated

parts.note: an avenue is a road

explanation.surface: Hailstones fall in the street for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like the weather but is the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is Latin for hail, a greeting, as in Ave Maria.

clue.text: Soldiers in heap — confusing situation

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the soldiers go within the heap

parts.note: a mass is a heap or pile
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers lying in a heap make for a messy scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, and figuratively a complicated situation that is hard to escape.

clue.text: Scene finally hidden by coastal fog certainly not the most pleasant

indicators.note: something hidden by a fog is enveloped in it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a sea mist is fog rolling in off the sea

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The last of a view vanishes into sea fog, making it far from pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamiest is the superlative of seamy, meaning sordid or unpleasant, the very opposite of most pleasant.
